text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet is expected to discuss today draft amendments to the Insurance law to fight local strong arm insurance companies.

Under the draft the minimum required capital for a licence will be raised ten-fold to two billion levs for life insurance companies and to 3.5 billion levs from 400 million levs for reinsurance companies. @
-- Bulgaria needs some 40 billion levs to counter 850 major landslides in the country, Trade minister Valentin Vasilev said.

Heavy rains, large buildups of underground water, lack of drainage and setting up of large buildings set off landslides this spring along the Bulgarian northern Black Sea coast which could affect the tourist season this summer.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet is expected to submit to parliament the country's draft budget in the next two weeks, deputy finance minister Dimitar Radev told the national radio.
-- A mission of the International Monetary Fund lead by IMF executive director Johannes Wejnholds arrived in Sofia to monitor the preparations to introduce a currency board system in the country.
-- Bulgaria's state gas monopolist Bulgargas said its daily losses amounted to some $300,000 because retailer surcharge of four percent for gas distributors was deemed low.
-- Bulgaria's northeast Black sea Albena holiday resort said it expected $3.5 million net profit this year.

-- Bulgarian customs officers said they have seized 0.220 kilogrammes of cocain worth some 25 million levs at the airport of Bulgaria's northeast Black Sea port of Varna. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
